claims.text: The strangler fig replaces an old system gradually: a routing layer in front of it sends one piece of the traffic at a time to new code, until nothing reaches the old part and it can be removed.
At stage-3 staff list failed refunds at GET /api/v1/refunds?status=failed; DonHang.Payments, with its own database donhang_payments, answers every request to /api/v1/refunds (§2, §8).
ADR 0008: the old tables notifications and payments still sit in database donhang at stage-3, unused by any code, left when Notifications and Payments got their own databases (ADR 0002, 0003).
Caddy has reverse-proxied /api/v1/* to DonHang.Api since stage-1, and the api publishes no port of its own, so every request from outside the Compose network under /api/v1/ passes through Caddy.
claims.source_hint: Caddyfile @ stage-1 lines 1-2, 22-24; docker-compose.yml @ stage-3 (api has no ports; lab publishes 8080/8443)

claims.text: After each move you check the system still works (e.g. the moved path answers real requests); a misbehaving piece is routed back, fixed and moved again. Moving back works only while the old code still answers that path, so the old part goes last.
claims.source_hint: outline items 3-4; inference from the mechanism

claims.text: A rewrite from scratch delivers nothing until the whole new system is finished and its single switch-over has no small step to undo; each strangler step leaves the system working and is small enough to undo.

Two Caddyfile sites serve /api/v1/ (:8080, donhang.local:8443); a third, :8180, proxies to Keycloak. In the :8080 site's route block (line 17), handle /api/v1/refunds* (lines 25-27) proxies to payments:8080, written before handle /api/v1/* (lines 28-30) to api:8080.

Inside a route block Caddy keeps directives in written order, and only the first matching handle block runs; so the refunds block wins because it comes first (not by specificity), and a new piece's block must go before line 28.
claims.source_hint: Caddy docs: Caddyfile directives (sorting), directives/route ('preserves the order'), directives/handle ('only the first matching')

claims.text: On staging, HTTPRoute api (namespace donhang) has a rule matching PathPrefix /api/v1, /api/v2, /openapi to Service api:8080 and a rule matching PathPrefix /api/v1/refunds (that path and the paths below it) to Service payments:8080.
Among HTTPRoute rules that match a request, Gateway API gives precedence to the longest matching path, so /api/v1/refunds wins over /api/v1.
claims.source_hint: Gateway API spec, HTTPRouteRule matches precedence (v1.6 standard channel)

claims.text: DonHang.Api never had a refunds endpoint: no code under DonHang.Api answers /api/v1/refunds at stage-2 or stage-3; the refunds list was new code in DonHang.Payments.
claims.source_hint: git grep -i refund stage-2 -- DonHang.Api (no hits); DonHang.Payments/RefundsController.cs @ stage-3

claims.text: ADR 0008: dump both tables (pg_dump -Fc --table), keep the file with other backups; drop notifications, then payments after accounting's check; each PR also drops the table from the TRUNCATE PostgresFixture.ResetAsync uses to empty every table between tests.

Debts N1 (old notifications table) and N2 (old payments table) in tech-debt-register.md: readers of the donhang schema think the API still sends email and keeps money records; both are paid by ADR 0008.

Trade-offs: strangler fig fits when the old part's traffic can be split; a rewrite fits only a part small enough to rebuild in one short step; changing code in place fits when the part stays where it is.

If the old part has no routing layer, add one first, sending everything to the old code; clients reach it because it takes over the address they call, or by one client change made once. A routing change moves requests, not data.
claims.source_hint: outline items 1-3; depth_notes (data sync deferred to backend.l4.expand-and-contract)

claims.text: Clients keep calling the same addresses, so a piece moves to new code, or back, by changing the routing layer alone, with no client release.
The donhang.local:8443 site has a single handle /api/v1/* block (lines 84-86) proxying to api:8080, so a refunds request over HTTPS reaches api, not payments.

Up to stage-2 DonHang.Api's DonHangDbContext mapped Payment to table payments in donhang; at stage-3 it maps neither Payment nor Notification, and the old payments and notifications tables stay in donhang, unread.

beyond_scope: Try it compares the :8443 HTTPS site, which does not route refunds to Payments; used to show that a piece has moved only where every routing layer sends it to new code.
